prospective_statement: Every relation, refusal, check and acceptance criterion in this file was written before any composition code existed and before any Slice 2C observation. No MLX operation, native bridge call, qualification child, composition path or Rust R1 was run while drafting it. The fixture population was produced by a stdlib-only generator whose only arithmetic is exact integer offset/size arithmetic and the frozen Slice 2B domain classifier; the generator's oracle does not call production slicing (mlx_affine::AffineTriple::expert_slice / row_slice) or the production decoder. One non-numerical sanity observation preceded this file and is disclosed: the committed fixture checkpoints were opened with the Slice 1 catalog (Checkpoint::open, QuantizationConfig::from_config_json, validate_catalog, classify_module) in a throwaway program that was not committed; it confirmed admission and the resolved (bits, group) of every module, that ck-a-single and ck-a-sibling have the same catalog digest, and that dropping the block.1.stack_d override is refused as InconsistentOverride with implied_bits 8. No range, byte or number from any selection or execution was observed.

correction_policy.rule_1: An observation that exceeds a bound, violates an exact invariant, or fails any acceptance criterion is a FAIL. It is recorded against the original criteria of the contract version under which it was observed and is retained permanently.
correction_policy.rule_2: Any revision of a relation, a refusal, an assumption, a check or an acceptance criterion is a new, separately identified contract version (new schema version string and file hash) that must be independently reviewed and explicitly authorized by the owner before any renewed qualification run.
correction_policy.rule_3: No appended entry, correction, erratum or replacement contract may convert a recorded failure into a pass, and no threshold is moved in place. A renewed qualification under a revised contract is a new run with its own evidence; the earlier failure remains a failure of the earlier version.
correction_policy.rule_4: The qualification report binds the sha256 of this contract file, the fixture manifest, the generator and the Slice 2B contract; a report produced under a different contract version cannot satisfy this version's acceptance criteria.
correction_policy.failure_triage: Every failed attempt is preserved with candidate commit and contract identity. An implementation defect gets a targeted fix and a separately identified rerun. A contract defect, a scope expansion, an unsupported prerequisite or a numerical-rule change is a STOP reported to the planner.

stages.what: Checkpoint::open(dir, OpenMode::Auto) (Slice 1 admission; catalog refusals unchanged and reported as C-R-CATALOG with the Slice 1 variant); QuantizationConfig::from_config_json(config.json); Checkpoint::hash_shards for the payload-inclusive source identity; the backing: one immutable host buffer per shard (optionally a manifest-declared prefix window) read through the catalog's admitted descriptors
stages.copies: the backing buffer is a copy of the shard file's bytes (fixture load)

stages.what: the Slice 1 resolution authority: classify_module(catalog, Some(config), module) -> ModuleKind::Quantized(AffineTriple); the spec is the explicit override when config.explicit(module) is Some, else the default. This resolved triple, never a caller-created one, is the authority for the recipe (bits, group size, mode, metadata dtype), for resolved_from (override iff config.explicit(module) is Some) and for slicing. A refusal is C-R-RESOLVE with the Slice 1 AffineError variant recorded

composition refusals C-R-SOURCE-BINDING .. C-R-BACKING in composition_refusals.order, then the Slice 1 checked selection RESOLVED_TRIPLE.expert_slice(index_path) giving the three absolute ranges, then borrowing the three ranges from the backing
stages.copies: none: the plane borrows &[u8] sub-slices of the immutable backing

stages.what: SelectedPlane (plane_identity) constructed once from one resolved triple and one index path
the independent selection checks S-IDENTITY, S-RANGES, S-BYTES against the manifest oracle, before any native call

staging into the existing Slice 2B HostTensor form: w U32 [N, K*bits/32], scales and biases in their stored dtype [N, K/group]; the packed weight is copied byte for byte, never unpacked or widened; S-STAGED-EQUAL
stages.copies: one byte copy per component of exactly the plane's bytes (plane_bytes), plus x from the standalone file

stages.what: the EXISTING Slice 2B bridge quantized_matmul on the staged tensors: Slice 2B refusals in their frozen order on host data, then OP-IMPORT (mlx_array_new_data copies), OP-CAST (mlx_astype of BF16 scales/biases to float32 on the explicit GPU stream), OP-QMM (mlx_quantized_matmul, transpose=true, the imported U32 weight passed unchanged), Evaluated readback
stages.copies: native import copies of x, w, scales, biases; two float32 metadata arrays from OP-CAST; one float32 output; one host readback copy of the output
B stages its own HostTensors from the standalone file; C reads the standalone file

entry_levels.E-COMPOSE: the full path P0-P7 from (checkpoint directory, config, module path, index path)
entry_levels.E-SELECT: the public selection function select_plane(checkpoint with its backing, QuantizationConfig, candidate AffineTriple, index path). The candidate triple is NEVER the authority: select_plane resolves the module named by the candidate through classify_module (C-R-RESOLVE on failure), requires the candidate's three TensorMeta to equal the resolved triple's and the catalog's authoritative entries (C-R-MODULE-BINDING), requires the candidate's QuantSpec (bits, group size, mode) and metadata dtype to equal the resolved ones (C-R-RECIPE-BINDING), and then slices with the RESOLVED triple. It must re-establish every binding itself because AffineTriple::new is public and accepts caller-supplied TensorMeta and QuantSpec
entry_levels.E-RANGE: the composition layer's own range resolution (absolute range -> borrowed slice of a backing), exercised directly by the overflow probe

fields.source_identity: sha256 of the `shasum -a 256` listing of the checkpoint's shard files in C-locale order (inside the checkpoint directory: LC_ALL=C shasum -a 256 *.safetensors | shasum -a 256); payload-inclusive, so two checkpoints with identical headers and catalog digests differ
fields.module: the module path, as an opaque string
fields.index_path: the selected expert index path (length = the number of leading dimensions, 1 here)
fields.ranges: weight, scales, biases: (shard file name, absolute begin, length) each
fields.logical_shape: [N, K] with K = packed_cols*32/bits from the RESOLVED spec
fields.transpose: true (y = x @ W^T, the Safetensors [out, in] layout)

invariants.statement: A SelectedPlane has exactly one index_path and exactly one source/module binding; its three ranges are derived inside one constructor from one resolved triple and that one index path. It has no public field, no setter, no constructor or builder that accepts per-component ranges, tensors or indices, and no way to replace one component of an existing plane. Weight from expert A cannot be combined with scales or biases from expert B, or from another module or source, through any public API.
invariants.verification: REQUIRED public-interface test (slice2c-plan.md section 2.2): (1) an API audit of the plane module's source: no pub or pub(crate) field, no Default or Clone, the only public functions returning a SelectedPlane are select_plane and compose (one index path and one triple or module each), no public function taking a ByteSlice, TripleSlice, raw range or component bytes, and no &mut self method; (2) every public entry (E-COMPOSE, E-SELECT) driven with cross-module and cross-source components must refuse (C-R-MODULE-BINDING, C-R-SOURCE-BINDING), and every accepted plane's three ranges must be those of the one requested index. Mutation controls mut-swap-scales and mut-swap-biases, injected at the selection-record level through the test-only child path, show that a mixed selection, if it ever arose, is detected by S-RANGES and S-BYTES before native execution

invariants.statement: the plane borrows its three byte ranges from the immutable backing (lifetime tied to the backing); it does not own copies; the backing is never mutated while any plane borrows it

no complete float32 (or any float) weight matrix of the plane is created on the QMM path; the packed U32 words are staged and imported unchanged (inherits native-primitives-v1.json#scope.packed_weight_path)
no unsafe reinterpretation (pointer casts, transmute, align_to, from_raw_parts) is used to avoid a copy; the library crate remains #![forbid(unsafe_code)]

composition_refusals.principle: Checked in this order, on host data, before any MLX-C call of the case (no import, no numerical call); the first failing check's id is returned as a typed error and the case records it. The inherited Slice 2B refusals then apply to the selected plane, in their frozen order, inside the existing bridge, also before any MLX-C numerical call or import.

order.condition: Slice 1 catalog admission fails (any catalog-contract.md refusal); the Slice 1 variant is recorded. No Slice 2C probe: the Slice 1 negative corpus already covers these and is not duplicated.

classify_module does not return Quantized for the module under the configuration (unknown module, incomplete triple, override inconsistent with the stored shapes, scales without configuration, ...); the Slice 1 AffineError variant and, for InconsistentOverride, implied_bits are recorded
the backing's source identity (shard file names and sha256 values, recorded when the backing was loaded) differs from the opened checkpoint's (Checkpoint::hash_shards provenance)

the candidate triple's weight, scales or biases TensorMeta is not the checkpoint catalog's authoritative entry for <module>.weight, <module>.scales, <module>.biases respectively, or differs from the resolved triple's (name and full TensorMeta equality)

the candidate triple's (bits, group size, mode, metadata dtype) differs from the recipe the resolution authority (QuantizationConfig + classify_module) resolves for the module. Probe ref-recipe-mismatch: block.0.stack_a's own three descriptors with the recipe 8-bit / group 32, which Slice 1 admits as shape-consistent (packed width 32, 4 groups, logical K 128) while the authority resolves 4-bit / group 64 (K 256) from the default; group 32 is also outside the Slice 2C scope. Without this refusal the plane would reach the Slice 2B bridge, whose domain admits 8-bit / group 32, and execute a misread weight
index_path length != the triple's number of leading dimensions
rank matches and some index >= its leading extent (including values near u64::MAX, which are never wrapped, truncated or narrowed)

a checked u64/usize operation of the composition layer's range arithmetic overflows (begin + len, begin or end conversion). Through an admitted catalog and a validated AffineTriple this is unreachable (catalog rules 10-12 and 24b; Slice 1 C-SLICE); the probe exercises E-RANGE directly
a selected range's end exceeds the length of the backing (window) of its shard, or the checkpoint has no backing (header-only)

composition_refusals.evaluation_rule: The generator evaluates every composition guard from C-R-RESOLVE on independently (manifest composition_refusal_order and oracle.composition_guards; C-R-CATALOG is omitted there because it has no Slice 2C probe and every fixture checkpoint is admissible); a guard whose precondition fails is recorded as not evaluable, BY NAME (never by position in the order). Every guard map's key set (evaluated union not evaluable) equals composition_refusal_order exactly; the generator asserts it on every run and its test checks it for all 26 guard maps. Every FX-COMP-REFUSE probe violates EXACTLY ONE evaluable guard, its expected id; every accepted and inherited-refusal case violates none.
composition_refusals.instrumentation: The child samples the existing MLX-C call counters (numerical, imports; crates/mlx-native-affine/src/bin/qualify/ffi.rs call_counts) at case start and at the refusal decision and records both deltas; for a composition refusal or a detected mutation the whole-case delta must be (0, 0). For inherited refusals the existing OpStats numerical_before_decision and imports_before_decision must be 0. The parent enforces both from the report.

selection_checks.principle: Exact comparisons of the candidate's selection against the manifest oracle, performed in the child before any native call (so a wrong plane is never executed) and re-decided by the parent from the reported values (the parent never trusts a child verdict).

checks.statement: every plane_identity field except ranges equals oracle.identity exactly
for each component: (shard file name, absolute begin, length) equals oracle.ranges exactly
for each component: sha256 of the borrowed bytes equals oracle.sha256 (the sha256 of the oracle's expected plane bytes, which are also the standalone file's w/scales/biases tensors)

A's staged HostTensors w, scales, biases and x are byte-identical, with identical dtype and shape, to B's HostTensors loaded from the standalone file, and both equal the manifest's expected.staged_inputs
checks.evidence: the child report carries, for A and for B separately and for each of w, scales, biases and x: dtype, shape, byte length and sha256 of the exact host bytes handed to mlx_array_new_data (the staged HostTensor bytes as imported). The parent decides S-STAGED-EQUAL from these records against expected.staged_inputs; it never accepts the child's verdict

checks.statement: the sha256 of every shard file and of every backing buffer, and of the standalone file, equals the manifest's expected.source_hashes at every phase
checks.evidence: the child report carries phase-labelled hashes: phase before_load (shard files, before Checkpoint::open and backing load; standalone file before B's load), phase after_host_selection (shard files and backing buffers with their lengths, after selection and staging, before any native call) and phase after_native_execution (shard files, backing buffers and the standalone file, after A and B). The parent decides S-SOURCE-UNCHANGED from these records

checks.statement: equal numerical outputs (N-COMP-AB, the R1 gates) never substitute for input-byte preservation: S-STAGED-EQUAL and S-SOURCE-UNCHANGED are decided from input evidence alone, and missing input evidence is a FAIL even when every output check passes

selection_checks.oracle_independence: oracle.ranges and oracle.sha256 are computed by the generator from the fixture specification (tensor placement chosen by its writer plus index * plane_bytes from (N, K, bits, group, dtype)) and cross-checked against a separate stdlib parse of the written headers and against slices of the written files; the test re-derives the ranges with its own header reader. None of them calls the Slice 1 slicing or decoding code.

comparisons.A: the composed path: E-COMPOSE, the plane's staged bytes through the existing bridge quantized_matmul
comparisons.B: the standalone plane: the oracle's expected w/scales/biases and x loaded from standalone/<id>.bin with the Slice 2B fixture loader, through the SAME bridge quantized_matmul, in the same child, on the same NativeContext and GPU stream, with the same bits, group size and transpose, immediately after A
comparisons.C: independent R1 on the oracle's expected logical data (the standalone file): the Rust binary64 R1 (crates/mlx-affine/src/reference_qmm.rs) and the exact Python R1 (scripts/research/mlx_affine_qmm_reference_v1.py), both unchanged

gates.rule: inherited unchanged: native-primitives-v1.json#acceptance_implementation, with n = the largest gamma_n in the case's families_0_31_2 and the both_references_rule; A and B are each decided against C independently
the float32 output bytes of A and B are identical, bit for bit, including the sign of zero, for every element
within one child, seq-aba-2's A output bytes equal seq-aba-0's A output bytes bit for bit (same selection, same x), with seq-aba-1 (another module at another bit width) executed between them

the BRIDGE-VISIBLE array handles of the composed path are exactly the manifest's array_census.bridge_visible_handles: four imports (x F32 [M,K], w U32 [N,K*bits/32], scales and biases BF16 [N,K/group]), two casts (scales_f32 and biases_f32 F32 [N,K/group]) and one output (F32 [M,N]); measured by counters in SEPARATE intervals, one opened immediately before and closed immediately after side A's bridge call and one likewise around side B's: each interval must show import counter delta 4, result handles created 3 and adopted 3, freed on an error path 0, array frees 7 (array_census.measured_counter_deltas.per_side.A and .B). The whole-case aggregate (A + B: 8 imports, 6 created, 6 adopted, 0 freed on an error path, 14 array frees for FX-COMP-ACCEPT and FX-COMP-SEQUENCE cases; array_census.measured_counter_deltas.whole_case_aggregate) is reported separately and must equal the sum of the two intervals; it is distinct from the whole-case refusal counters of FX-COMP-REFUSE and FX-COMP-MUTATION cases (0 imports, 0 numerical calls) and from the inherited-refusal counters (numerical_before_decision 0, imports_before_decision 0 per side). Also measured: the import records of S-STAGED-EQUAL and the output's Evaluated readback dtype and shape; the casts' dtype and shape are source-derived from the bridge's call (qmm_inner astype_f32). No bridge-visible float array of the weight's logical shape exists.
gates.internal_workspace: MLX-internal allocations are not bridge-visible and are NOT measured. They are disclosed as source-derived accounting in array_census.source_derived_workspace: for the 8 matrix cases, qmm_splitk's float32 intermediate of shape [split_k, M, N] (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:810-820), holding per-partition partial OUTPUT sums; it is not a weight matrix. The split-K sum uses strided_reduce_small (split_k < 32, MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/reduce.cpp:931-933), which allocates nothing; the vector-family kernels allocate nothing beyond the output; row-contiguous inputs are not copied

a_vs_b_relation.relation: EXACT BITWISE EQUALITY (N-COMP-AB). No tolerance is defined and none may be substituted.
premises: Identical inputs: S-STAGED-EQUAL establishes byte-identical x, w, scales, biases with identical dtypes and shapes before either execution.

Identical operation and settings: both go through the one existing bridge entry (quantized_matmul, transpose=true, same bits, group size, OP-CAST on the same explicit GPU stream of the same NativeContext, default device GPU), in the same child process, adjacent in time, with MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 (A-NONAX).

Identical kernel: QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu chooses the kernel only from transpose, M, N, K, the batch count, bits, group size, x dtype and the device (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:1386-1454; get_qmv_batch_limit depends on K, N and the device); qmm_splitk's split_k depends only on M, N, K and group size (quantized.cpp:787-803). Every input is made row-contiguous by the same rule (ensure_row_contiguous_matrix, quantized.cpp:1393-1400), and mlx_array_new_data imports are already row-contiguous, so no conditional copy distinguishes A from B.

No order-dependent accumulation visible in source: there is no atomic operation in MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h or mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp; the split-K partial sums are written to an intermediate array (quantized.cpp:810-820) by distinct threadgroups and reduced by strided_reduce_general_dispatch (quantized.cpp:860-866), whose column-reduce kernels write each output non-atomically (mlx/backend/metal/kernels/reduction/reduce_col.h:86-90, 139, 250-254, 283-287, 390-394; that file contains no atomic operation). The only floating-point atomic add, Sum::atomic_update (kernels/reduction/ops.h:130-131), is reached from the scatter kernels (kernels/indexing/scatter.h:57, scatter_axis.h:51), not from this path.

Under D-GEOM every element of the split-K intermediate and of the output is written before it is read (N % 64 == 0 alignment, native-primitives-v1.json#domains.D-GEOM.justification.N_mod_64), so uninitialised allocator memory cannot reach a result.
a_vs_b_relation.failure_policy: A single differing bit in any element is a FAIL of N-COMP-AB, recorded for that case and contract version and never reclassified. Triage, without retry: if S-STAGED-EQUAL or S-BYTES failed, it is an implementation defect (targeted fix, separately identified rerun). If every input check passed and A and B still differ, A-DET is falsified for this build and host: STOP and report to the planner; replacing bitwise equality by any tolerance or by the R1 gates alone is a new contract version (correction_policy.rule_2). A and B must each still pass the inherited R1 gates against C; passing those never excuses an N-COMP-AB failure.

A-DET.statement: On one device, in one process, the same compiled Metal pipeline dispatched with the same grid and threadgroup geometry on byte-identical, identically shaped and identically strided input buffers produces byte-identical outputs. In particular simd_sum, quad_sum (MLX312:quantized.h:742, 809, 913, 969) and simdgroup_multiply_accumulate (A-MMA) evaluate in an order that, although unknown (U4, U5), is fixed for a given pipeline and input, and results do not depend on buffer addresses or on threadgroup scheduling order.
A-DET.basis: Not provable from pinned source: the order of the hardware reductions is not specified (native-primitives-v1.json U4, U5). The source-visible sources of run-to-run variation (atomics, kernel choice, conditional copies, uninitialised reads) are excluded by the premises of comparisons.a_vs_b_relation.
A-DET.if_false: N-COMP-AB fails; the failure policy applies. The inherited bounds are unaffected (they are order-independent).

copy_and_ownership.accounting_method: Two kinds of entry are kept apart everywhere in copy and lifetime reporting and are labelled in the report. MEASURED: host buffers the child allocates or copies (role, dtype, shape, bytes, sha256 of staged bytes), borrowed ranges (begin, length, backing shard; reported as borrows, not copies), and counter deltas (imports, result handles created/adopted/freed on error, array frees, numerical calls) in separate intervals around side A's and side B's bridge call, plus the separately reported whole-case aggregate (N-COMP-ARRAYS). SOURCE-DERIVED: the dtype and shape of the two cast results (from the bridge's code) and MLX-internal workspace (array_census.source_derived_workspace, from pinned MLX source); these are declared from source, never presented as observations. The parent compares measured entries with array_census.bridge_visible_handles and measured_counter_deltas (N-COMP-ARRAYS) and with the component plane_bytes.

stages.fixture_load: one immutable host buffer per shard (a prefix window when the manifest declares one); the only copy of source bytes before staging
stages.host_selection: borrowed &[u8] sub-slices of the backing; zero copies
stages.staging: one copy of exactly plane_bytes[component] into each Slice 2B HostTensor (the bridge API takes owned HostTensors; changing that API is not authorized)
stages.metadata_widening: OP-CAST creates two float32 arrays of the metadata shape [N, K/group] only (handles measured by counter; dtype/shape source-derived)
stages.execution: one float32 output [M, N]; the packed U32 weight is consumed unchanged; the kernels decode codes transiently (native-primitives-v1.json#scope.packed_weight_path)
stages.readback: one host copy of the output through the Evaluated typestate (E2)

copy_and_ownership.lifetimes: backing outlives every plane that borrows it; HostTensors are owned by the case; NativeArray<'ctx> handles are dropped before the case ends (zero live arrays between cases, as in Slice 2B)
prohibited: a complete float weight matrix on the QMM path
mutation of the backing while borrowed

mutation_controls.principle: A mutation control proves that the independent checks are SENSITIVE to one specific selection defect. The harness injects the defect at the selection-record level through a test-only path of the child (never through a public plane constructor): it replaces the named ranges or identity fields of the record, reads the bytes at the mutated ranges from the backing, and submits the mutated record to the same checks. Every listed check, and no other, must report a mismatch (the detection set is exactly the set of mismatches the specified mutation causes; the generator and its test assert exact set equality), the mutation must have taken effect exactly as the manifest specifies (the mutated ranges and sha256 equal composition.mutation.ranges/sha256), and no native call is issued in the case. A control that is not detected, or detected by a different set of checks, is a FAIL.

controls.defect: selection arithmetic uses expert (e+1) mod E while the identity records e
weight plane stride one u32 word too large on expert 2 of 4 (stays inside the tensor; invisible on expert 0 by construction)
scales of expert 2 with weight and biases of expert 3
biases of expert 0 with weight and scales of expert 1 (three shards)
the 8-bit override is dropped from the configuration
the plane records the 4-bit default for an 8-bit-override module, so bits (8 -> 4) and resolved_from (override -> default) both change; ranges and bytes unchanged

mutation_controls.detectability_precondition: Every expert of every module has pairwise-distinct packed weights, scales and biases (asserted by the generator and the test), so a range defect that selects another expert's component changes that component's bytes.
mutation_controls.not_claimed: Arbitrary corrupted bytes are NOT claimed detectable without an identity or reference check: a byte change inside a correctly selected range is detected only by S-BYTES against the oracle hash (fixtures) or by the R1 gates, and in production (no oracle) only by a payload identity such as a verified shard sha256. Mutations are not claimed to cover every possible selection defect.

acceptance_criteria_slice_2c: C1: the frozen population validates (generator --check; manifest, file and listing hashes) before and after the run; the generator test passes.

C2: every FX-COMP-ACCEPT and FX-COMP-SEQUENCE case: S-IDENTITY, S-RANGES, S-BYTES, S-STAGED-EQUAL and S-SOURCE-UNCHANGED decided by the parent from the report's input evidence (S-NO-OUTPUT-SUBSTITUTION), N-COMP-ARRAYS on measured counters, N-QMM-SHAPE-DTYPE(A and B), N-COMP-AB, G-QMM-EXACT and G-QMM-RUST for A and for B against C, G-R1-SELF-QMM on C; family, split_k and gamma exponent recorded.
C3: N-COMP-ABA on seq-aba-2 against seq-aba-0.
C4: every FX-COMP-REFUSE case refused with exactly its expected C-R id and a whole-case MLX-C call delta of (0 numerical, 0 imports).

C5: every FX-COMP-INHERITED-REFUSE case: selection checks pass, then A and B are refused by the existing bridge with exactly the expected Slice 2B id, numerical_before_decision = 0 and imports_before_decision = 0.
C6: every FX-COMP-MUTATION case detected by exactly its detected_by checks (exact set equality), the mutation applied exactly as specified, and no native call in the case.

C7: I-PLANE-SINGLE-INDEX by its required public-interface test; I-PLANE-NO-REINTERPRET verified statically; I-PLANE-NO-F32-WEIGHT through N-COMP-ARRAYS; the library crate stays MLX-free and #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; the child still contains exactly one mlx_set_error_handler call site and no newly linked crate calls it. Independence of the child from R1 and from the production decoder at two levels: (a) a static test that no child code path (src/compose.rs, src/frozen_compose.rs, src/bin/qualify/**) names mlx_affine reference, reference_qmm, qmm_reference, dq_reference, decode, dequantize_rows or unpack_codes, and that none glob-imports mlx_affine; (b) an nm check of the built qualify executable: no symbol containing 10mlx_affine13reference_qmm, 10mlx_affine9reference or 10mlx_affine6decode; a positive control (at least one 10mlx_affine6module symbol present); and a negative control (the same scan of the parent test executable, which calls reference_qmm, finds 10mlx_affine13reference_qmm).
C8: E1-E4 and E6 in the compose child on the required gate host; E5 recorded; cleanup accounting clean; parent failure conditions and watchdog as in Slice 2B.

C9: execution.slice_2b_regression.primary_b_same_run_differential holds in full (canonical child reports equal after removing exactly V1-V4, identical gate counts equal to attempt 3, identical test-name list); secondary_a_cross_run is performed and recorded, and any mismatch in it is reported to the planner.
C10: the composition step is required in apple-mlx-small-fixtures through doctor X/Y, and every doctor mutation control of reporting_and_ci.ci is rejected.
